# Not a score. An argument.

> A detector for AI-generated and manipulated images that answers in prose
> rather than with a probability. Upload a photograph and two vision-language
> models each write what they found in it. Built by a five-person KAUST
> Academy team, August 2026.

Most detectors output a score. A score of 0.83 gives an editor nothing to
check, cite, or appeal. This one outputs an argument: the verdict is a
sentence inside a written explanation of what the model saw.

## The two models

- **Our fine-tune** — LoRA adapters on the released checkpoint, 4-bit,
  greedy decoding, reproducible, 9.9s warm inference.
- **Original (PRIS-CV)** — the published checkpoint at FP16, sampled at
  temperature 0.2, different wording on every run, 15.6s warm inference.

The fine-tune has no public name yet. Do not invent one.

## Attribution

Built on the base checkpoint `AnnaGao/FakeReasoning` by PRIS-CV. The team's
contribution is LoRA adapters on those weights: 62,586,880 trainable
parameters, 0.799% of the model. This is not a model trained from scratch.

## Measured results

- 92.5% accuracy across ten unseen generators, unchanged by fine-tuning
- Class separation +0.520, up from +0.274
- In-distribution accuracy 64.0% to 72.0%
- Fake recall 51.7%, real recall 100.0%
- The fine-tune answers "real" 70% of the time

The accuracy point estimates come from small samples — n=50
in-distribution, four images per generator — and should not be quoted
without that caveat. Class separation and the prior shift are the findings
the authors consider robust at this scale.

## The known weakness

Fake recall fell to 51.7% while real recall reached 100.0%. A fake verdict
from this model is therefore stronger evidence than a real one. This is
stated on the page next to the verdict, not hidden in a footnote.

## What the system does not produce

- No confidence score, percentage, meter, or gauge. One was built and
  deliberately removed for being unfaithful to the model.
- No heatmap, attention overlay, or bounding box. Nothing in the response
  is spatial.
- No verdict other than "real" or "fake". There is no uncertain state.

## Timing

Warm inference is 9.9s for the fine-tune and 15.6s for the official model.
Both scale to zero after five idle minutes, so a visitor arriving after a
quiet period pays a cold start and can wait up to about a minute. The site
never describes itself as real-time or instant.
